comment: Host profiles for the off-platform gate. Each entry says what the host is, how to build its prelude, and what an artifact must do there. `shim` prepends tools/roblog.lua (a genuine-DataModel Roblox host). `expect` is either 'run' (payload must print) or 'stop' (payload must never print). Profiles whose id starts with 'roblox-' or that describe an attached debugger model a genuine client's real quirks (locked metatables, a shared _G, a reduced debug table) and must run.

profiles.label: bare Luau interpreter
profiles.why: No game, no Instance, no task: the first gate line already fails.

profiles.label: Lune-like runtime (Luau without Roblox)
profiles.why: Luau libraries are present but nothing from the Roblox API is.
profiles.prelude: local game,workspace,Instance,Enum,task,typeof=nil,nil,nil,nil,nil,nil

profiles.label: Lua 5.1 host wearing a Luau hat
profiles.why: _VERSION says Lua, table.create/freeze and bit32 are absent.
profiles.prelude: local _VERSION="Lua 5.1" local table={insert=table.insert,remove=table.remove,concat=table.concat,sort=table.sort,unpack=table.unpack,getn=table.getn} local bit32=nil local utf8=nil local typeof=nil

profiles.label: table posing as game
profiles.why: typeof(game) is 'table'; a DataModel is never a plain table. The fake is installed in the environment, which is what the loader reads - a local shadow cannot reach it any more now that the gate names nothing.
profiles.prelude: do local E=getfenv(1) E.game={ClassName="DataModel",Parent=nil,GetChildren=function() return {} end,GetService=function() return {} end,FindFirstChild=function() end} E.workspace={} end

profiles.label: Instance that is not a DataModel
profiles.why: Real typeof, real Instance, wrong class name, installed in the environment.
profiles.prelude: do local E=getfenv(1) E.game=Instance.new("Part") end

profiles.label: GetService that invents services
profiles.why: GetService invents services instead of refusing unknown ones, installed in the environment.
profiles.prelude: do local E=getfenv(1) local raw=E.game E.game=setmetatable({ClassName="DataModel",Parent=nil},{__index=function(_,k) if k=="GetService" then return function() return {} end end return raw[k] end}) end

profiles.label: Luau before table.create (pre-0.5.1 Roblox)
profiles.why: Luau before table.create (pre-0.5.1 Roblox), installed in the environment.
profiles.prelude: do local E=getfenv(1) E.table={freeze=table.freeze,unpack=table.unpack,insert=table.insert,concat=table.concat,sort=table.sort,remove=table.remove} end

profiles.label: typeof that lies
profiles.why: typeof that answers like type, so a real Instance reads as a table, installed in the environment.
profiles.prelude: do local E=getfenv(1) E.typeof=function(v) return type(v) end end

profiles.label: a swapped global string library no longer stops the payload
profiles.why: 0.17.0 parked here, and that check is what froze every real Roblox client: Roblox locks built-in metatables, so the identity comparison could never hold there. The payload no longer needs it - every string helper is captured into a local at load, so a library swapped afterwards is simply never called. Kept as a profile so the decision stays visible.
profiles.prelude: local s={} for k,v in next,string do s[k]=v end s.dump=function() return "" end local string=s

profiles.label: a shadow _G carrying a swapped library no longer stops the payload
profiles.why: _G is shared between scripts in a real game, so judging the host by what it contains was always unsound. Nothing reads _G now; the profile stays as the regression guard for that decision.
profiles.prelude: local g={} for k,v in next,_G do g[k]=v end local s={} for k,v in next,g.string do s[k]=v end g.string=s _G=g

profiles.label: genuine Roblox host (DataModel shim)
profiles.why: Everything the gate asks for is real, so the payload must run.

profiles.label: proxied DataModel
profiles.why: Proxied DataModel in the environment: the proxy answers every name, so only a behavioural check catches it.
profiles.prelude: do local E=getfenv(1) local raw=E.game E.game=setmetatable({ClassName=raw.ClassName,Parent=raw.Parent},{__index=function(_,k) return raw[k] end}) end

profiles.label: genuine Roblox host with a wrapped task library
profiles.why: Client-side libraries get wrapped all the time; the gate only reads through them, so the payload must run.
profiles.prelude: local raw=task local task=setmetatable({},{__index=function(_,k) return raw[k] end})

profiles.label: genuine Roblox, locked built-in metatables
profiles.why: Roblox locks the metatables of strings, numbers and functions, so getmetatable("x") hands back the string 'This metatable is locked' instead of a table. A 0.17.0 check compared that against the string library and parked every real client - this profile keeps that from coming back.
profiles.prelude: local __gm=getmetatable getmetatable=function(v) local t=type(v) if t=="string" or t=="number" or t=="boolean" or t=="function" then return "The metatable is locked" end return __gm(v) end

profiles.label: genuine Roblox, _G written by another script
profiles.why: _G is shared between all scripts in a game, so another script may have replaced or stubbed entries in it. The gate must not judge the host by what it finds there.
profiles.prelude: local _G={string={},table={},typeof=function() return nil end,game=nil,print=function() end}

profiles.label: genuine Roblox, client debug library
profiles.why: The Roblox client debug table has info/traceback/profilebegin and no gethook, which is exactly the surface Luau clients provide.
profiles.prelude: local debug={info=debug.info,traceback=debug.traceback,profilebegin=function() end,profileend=function() end}

profiles.label: genuine Roblox with a debugger or profiler attached
profiles.why: Studio and the profiler install a debug hook, so debug.gethook() is non-nil during a perfectly legitimate run. Treating a hook as tampering poisoned real sessions.
profiles.prelude: local __hw=function() end if debug.gethook~=nil then debug.gethook=function() return __hw end end

profiles.label: host that defines a global named _ENV
profiles.why: On Luau `_ENV` is an ordinary global name, not a language feature, so any host can define it. 0.18.0 used to read it before getfenv and would capture itself into whatever table the host supplied - the payload then ran into a fake global table and printed nothing. The loader now validates every candidate and prefers getfenv on any host that has it.
profiles.prelude: local _ENV=setmetatable({},{__index=function() return 1 end,__call=function(t) return t end})

profiles.label: host with no usable script environment
profiles.why: getfenv is gone and both _G and _ENV are empty tables. The artifact must say so with a named error; a silent return is what 'no output from Luau' looked like from the outside.
profiles.prelude: local getfenv=nil local _G={} local _ENV={}

profiles.label: host that wraps pcall in Lua and forwards every call
profiles.why: A forwarding wrapper keeps pcall's behaviour, so a check that only calls pcall cannot see it. The chain asks debug.info where pcall came from, and a Lua closure wearing pcall's name is not a builtin.
profiles.prelude: do local E=getfenv(1) local raw=E.pcall E.pcall=function(...) return raw(...) end end

profiles.label: host that wraps getfenv in Lua and forwards every call
profiles.why: The classic way to hand a loader a doctored environment: wrap getfenv, answer with a table of your choosing. Forwarding it faithfully keeps every behavioural check green, so the provenance check is what catches it.
profiles.prelude: do local E=getfenv(1) local raw=E.getfenv E.getfenv=function(...) return raw(...) end end

profiles.label: host with debug.info taken away
profiles.why: Luau always ships debug.info. A host that has debug but not info has had it removed, which is exactly what an executor does before it starts hooking things.
profiles.prelude: do local E=getfenv(1) local d={} for k,v in next,E.debug do d[k]=v end d.info=nil E.debug=d end

profiles.label: host whose Instance.new hands back a table
profiles.why: Instance.new is the most replaced function in a faked Roblox client: returning a table with the right ClassName satisfied every name-based check this tool used to make. It no longer satisfies the type one.
profiles.prelude: do local E=getfenv(1) E.Instance=setmetatable({new=function(cls) return {ClassName=cls,Parent=nil} end},{__index=E.Instance}) end

profiles.label: GetService that hands out a fresh handle every call
profiles.why: A service is a singleton: game:GetService("Players") is one object for the life of the session, FindFirstChild agrees with it, and IsA agrees with its ClassName. A host that builds a new table per call satisfies every name-based test and fails all three of these.
profiles.prelude: do local E=getfenv(1) local real=E.game local mt=getmetatable(real) E.game=setmetatable({ClassName="DataModel",Name="Game",Parent=nil,GetService=function(self,name) local s=real.GetService(real,name) return setmetatable({ClassName=s.ClassName,Name=s.Name},{__index=function(_,k) return s[k] end}) end,GetChildren=function(self) return real.GetChildren(real) end,FindFirstChild=function(self,name) return real.FindFirstChild(real,name) end,IsA=function(self,n) return n=="DataModel" or n=="Instance" end},mt) end

profiles.label: DataModel whose child list is padded with tables
profiles.why: Every child of the DataModel is a service, so every child must be an Instance parented to the DataModel. A host with a long child list and only a few real services is a table of handles with a list bolted on.
profiles.prelude: do local E=getfenv(1) local real=E.game local mt=getmetatable(real) local GetChildren=function(self) return real.GetChildren(real) end E.game=setmetatable({ClassName="DataModel",Name="Game",Parent=nil,GetService=function(self,name) return real.GetService(real,name) end,GetChildren=function(self) local k=GetChildren(self) local out={} for i=1,#k do out[i]=k[i] end for i=1,12 do out[#out+1]={ClassName="Part",Name="Ghost"..i,Parent=self} end return out end,FindFirstChild=function(self,name) return real.FindFirstChild(real,name) end,IsA=function(self,n) return n=="DataModel" or n=="Instance" end},mt) end

profiles.label: Instance.new that invents classes
profiles.why: A real Instance.new raises on a class that does not exist. A host that answers every class name with a table cannot be asked what a class is, so the artifact has to ask it for one that is not a class.
profiles.prelude: do local E=getfenv(1) local I=E.Instance local raw=I.new I.new=function(cls,parent) local ok,inst=pcall(raw,cls,parent) if ok then return inst end return {ClassName=cls,Parent=parent} end end

profiles.label: replayed environment (tables)
profiles.why: Every API answered, every name right - but the instances are tables, because a log records answers, not an engine. `type(game)` is "table", `rawget` succeeds, `ClassName` is writable: the artifact refuses it.

profiles.label: transparent logger
profiles.why: Records every call and forwards it to the genuine host unchanged. Nothing here is a lie, so the artifact is expected to run: what these checks buy is that a *replay* of the recording does not.
profiles.prelude: local __log={} local __gs=game.GetService game.GetService=function(self,n) __log[#__log+1]=n local ok,v=pcall(__gs,self,n) if ok then return v end error(v,0) end local __in=Instance.new Instance.new=function(...) __log[#__log+1]='new' return __in(...) end
